rows.additional_description_1:
Bronx County (Bronx) - The Federal Highway Administration (FHWA), the New York State Department of Transportation (NYSDOT), as joint lead agencies, and the New York City Department of Transportation (NYC DOT), as project sponsor and joint lead agency, have made available the Draft Design Report (DDR) / NEPA Draft Environmental Impact Statement (DEIS) for the Shore Road Bridge over the Hutchinson River Project. In compliance with SEQRA/CEQR, the NYC DOT has also prepared additional documentation to cover topics not addressed in the DDR/NEPA DEIS.

The purpose of the Project is to address the structural deficiencies; geometric deficiencies; and operational reliability for multi-modal users, including marine vessels, of the Shore Road Bridge over the Hutchinson River. The existing Shore Road Bridge is over 115 years old and is an 865-foot-long bridge with seven spans. The main span over the navigation channel is a double-leaf movable bascule span, which opens for the passage of marine vessels. The bridge is located within Pelham Bay Park between the Bronx and Pelham Parkway and City Island Road along Shore Road in the Borough of Bronx, New York.

As a project requiring FHWA approval, the Project is subject to the requirements of Section 4(f) of the USDOT Act of 1966 (now codified in 23 USC §138 and 49 USC §303), and the FHWA implementing regulation, 23 CFR Part 774. In accordance with the applicable regulations and as documented in the DEIS, the FHWA intends to make a de minimis impact finding for the Section 4(f) use of Pelham Bay Park and the Pelham Bay Park Preserve.  The FHWA is soliciting comments from the public on the proposed de minimis impact determination for Pelham Bay Park and the Pelham Bay Park Preserve.

Two in-person public hearings will be held to provide information and receive comments on the DDR/NEPA DEIS and SEQRA/CEQR documentation. The same content will be presented at both hearings.  One will be held on Thursday, October 1, 2026, from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 pm at the Bartow Older Adult Center (Co-Op City) located at 2049 Bartow Avenue, Bronx, NY 10475 (Parking: Parking Garage 4, 99 Asch Loop, Bronx, NY 10475). The second will be held on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. at the Pelham Bay & Split Rock Golf Courses located at 870 Shore Road, Bronx, NY 10464 (parking available on site). Hearings will begin in an open-house format followed by a presentation and formal comment session for people who have signed up at the hearing to speak. Please submit any special accommodation requests by calling or emailing the contact below by 4:00 p.m., Monday, September 21, 2026. An on-demand presentation will also be available through the Project website after the completion of the in-person hearings.

 

Both the DDR/ NEPA DEIS and the SEQRA/CEQR Documentation are available at the Project website beginning September 4, 2026: https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/infrastructure/shoreroadbridge.shtml

Digital and/or physical copies will be available at the following locations:

Pelham Bay Public Library: 3060 Middletown Road, Bronx, NY 10461;

Baychester Library: 2049 Asch Loop, Bronx, NY 10475; and

City Island Public Library: 320 City Island Avenue, Bronx, NY 10464.

Public comments on the SEQRA/CEQR Documentation, DDR/NEPA DEIS and the proposed Section 4(f) de minimis impact determination must be received by November 2, 2026.  Following the close of the public comment period, FHWA, NYSDOT and NYC DOT will review and consider comments received.

Contact: Joannene Kidder, NYC DOT, 55 Water Street, 5th Floor, New York, NY 10041, Phone: (929) 505-1002, E-mail: ShoreRoadBridgeBX@dot.nyc.gov

COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT PROGRAM - DISASTER RECOVERY

PUBLIC NOTICE OF AVAILABILITY

NOTICE OF A PUBLIC HEARING

 

TO ALL INTERESTED RESIDENTS, GROUPS, COMMUNITY BOARDS, AND AGENCIES:

On Monday, September 14, 2026, the City of New York will release a substantial amendment to its Community Development Block Grant-Disaster Recovery (CDBG-DR) Action Plan for Hurricane Ida Recovery. Through this amendment, the City will detail its proposed use of $86,000,000 in reallocated CDBG-DR funding provided through the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD).

To access the plan beginning September 14, 2026, please visit: https://www.nyc.gov/site/cdbgdr/hurricane-ida/ida-action-plan.page. Executive Summaries will be available in English, Spanish, Chinese, Russian, Bengali, Haitian, Korean, Arabic, Urdu, French, and Polish. The online materials will also be accessible for the visually impaired. Paper copies of the Action Plan, including in large print format (18pt. font size), will be provided upon request.

The substantial amendment is subject to a 30-day public comment period, which will begin on September 15, 2026. Comments must be received no later than Friday, October 16, 2026 at 11:59 P.M. (EST). Written comments may be submitted to CDBGComments@omb.nyc.gov or to the Mayors Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Attention: Evan Pellegrino, Director of Community Development, 255 Greenwich Street, 8th Floor, New York, New York 10007.

A hearing is scheduled for October 8, 2026 from 6:00-7:00pm to obtain comments on the City's use of federal funds. The hearing may be attended either in person or virtually. Information for attending the hearing virtually or in person is below:

ZOOM link for virtual participation:

https://us06web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_fK1Fx3ylR5OpGKLrWtmhBA

Webinar ID: 897 3335 4124

Passcode: 1

Location for in person participation:

NYC City Planning Commission Hearing Room

120 Broadway, Lower Concourse

New York, New York 10002 

 

Please inform NYC Department of City Planning if you need reasonable accommodation or foreign language interpretation services, such as but not limited to sign language interpretation, to participate in the public hearing. Foreign language interpretation will be provided based on available resources. Please email requests to accessibilityinfo@planning.nyc.gov or call 212-720-3366 at least five business days before the hearing.

 

At the end of the comment period, all comments shall be reviewed, and City responses will be incorporated into the final Action Plan. The final Ida Action Plan, containing a summary of the comments and the City's responses, will be submitted to HUD and posted on the City's CDBG-DR website.

 

City of New York:      Zohran Kwame Mamdani, Mayor

rows.additional_description_1:
PLEASE TAKE NOTICE that a public hearing will be held on October 14, 2026 at 10:00 a.m., or as soon thereafter as the matter may be reached on the calendar, at which time those wishing to be heard will be given an opportunity to be heard concerning the proposed disposition of the real property identified below. The public hearing will be held via conference call. Call in #: 1-646-992-2010; Access Code 717 876 299

 

Pursuant to Section 695(2)(b) of the General Municipal Law and Section 1802(6)(j) of the Charter, the Department of Housing Preservation and Development ('HPD') of the City of New York ('City') has proposed the sale of the following City-owned property (collectively, 'Disposition Area') in the Borough of Brooklyn:

 

Address                                     Block/Lot(s)

435 Locke Street                        4445/ 50     

1050 Ashford Street                    4446/ 1     

1 Gateway Dr                              4445/ 1    (Formerly Block 4445, p/o Lot 1 and Block 4446, p/o Lot 1)

 

Under HPD's New Construction Finance Program, sponsors purchase City-owned or privately owned land or vacant buildings and construct multifamily buildings in order to create affordable rental housing.  Construction and permanent financing is provided through loans from private institutional lenders and from public sources including HPD, the New York City Housing Development Corporation, the State of New York, and the federal government. Additional funding may also be provided from the syndication of low-income housing tax credits. The newly constructed buildings provide rental housing affordable to low- and moderate-income households, with at least 60% of units affordable to households earning up to 80% of Area Median Income (AMI) and up to 40% of units affordable to households earning up to 120% of AMI. At least 15% of units are set aside for formerly homeless households.

 

Under the proposed project, the City will sell the Disposition Area to Nehemiah Spring Creek 5B Housing Development Fund Corporation ('Sponsor') for the nominal price of one dollar per tax lot. The Sponsor will also deliver an enforcement note and mortgage for the remainder of the appraised value (Land Debt). The Sponsor will then construct three buildings containing up to 200 rental dwelling units, including one superintendent unit, on the Disposition Area.

 

The Land Debt or the Citys capital subsidy may be repayable out of resale or refinancing profits for a period of at least thirty (30) years following completion of construction. The remaining balance, if any, may be forgiven at the end of the term.

 

The appraisal and the proposed Land Disposition Agreement and Project Summary are available for public examination by emailing Margaret Carey at careym@hpd.nyc.gov on business days during business hours.

 

To make a request for accommodation, such as sign language interpretation services, please contact the Mayors Office of Contract Services (MOCS) via e-mail at disabilityaffairs@mocs.nyc.gov or via phone at (212) 298-0734.  TDD users should call Verizon relay services.  Any person requiring reasonable accommodation for the public hearing should contact MOCS at least three business days in advance of the hearing to ensure availability.

Under HPD's Division of Property Disposition and Finance program, City-owned vacant and/or occupied multifamily residential buildings may be purchased and gut-rehabilitated by a designated sponsor in order to create affordable rental housing units with a range of affordability. Construction and permanent financing is provided through loans from private institutional lenders and from public sources, including HPD.

Pursuant to Section 695(2)(b) of the General Municipal Law and Section 1802(6)(j) of the Charter, the Department of Housing Preservation and Development ('HPD') of the City of New York ('City') proposed amendments to the terms and conditions of the sale of certain real property previously conveyed by the City of New York (collectively, 'Disposition Area') in the Borough of Manhattan:

                Address                            Block/Lots         Community District

                204 West 121 Street          1926/35                    10

Under HPD's Division of Property Disposition and Finance program, City-owned vacant and/or occupied multifamily residential buildings may be purchased and gut-rehabilitated by a designated sponsor in order to create affordable rental housing units with a range of affordability. Construction and permanent financing is provided through loans from private institutional lenders and from public sources, including HPD.

On November 23, 2020, the City conveyed the Disposition Area to CLT East Harlem/El Barrio Community Land Trust Housing Development Fund Corporation. The deed and land disposition agreement recorded against the Premises requires compliance with a project summary approved by the Council requiring the development of approximately 36 rental dwelling units, two commercial spaces, and one community facility space. While it was originally intended that there would be commercial spaces in the project, it is now being developed with three community facility spaces and approximately 38 rental dwelling units. On July 16, 2026 (Res. No. 579), the Council approved and amended project summary reflecting these new conditions, and the deed and land disposition agreement will be amended to reflect these changes.
